scope: Proposition 9.4 (Deep comparison) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 100. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a mixed Sobolev comparison order k ≥ 10. For every sufficiently small fixed δ2 > 0, one may fix ε0 > 0 and then ν0 > 0 sufficiently small as follows. Suppose the exact reduced-equation Cauchy jets on s = 0 satisfy the vacuum constraints and wave-map gauge, agree with g for v < (1 − ν0)T, and differ from the jets of g + hp by at most e−7κT/2 in Hk+1 × Hk (dx dθ). (9.9) Then these data have an exact vacuum development g′ on (P1), with normalized error F = g′ −g−hp bounded in the through-k mixed energies by Ce(κ+δ2)T ( e−7κT/2 + AT λ−M1 p + A2 T λP∗ p ) . (P7) The conclusion holds when this bound has a fixed exponential margin below AT and the required base packet norms are sufficiently exponentially small. The same estimate, with fixed buffers, controls normalized C2 error.
